lxc_6fb0a03e6501203c.text: Imagine sitting down in a busy Cologne brewery pub.

lxc_f7661248cf00bfa3.text: Before you even order, a waiter puts a small glass of beer in front of you.

lxc_506191f2d3468dfd.text: In North Rhine-Westphalia, beer is a local identity.

lxc_5a1f01b18964e0d8.text: Before your trip, you will learn what Kölsch, Altbier and Dortmunder Export are, and where they came from.

lxc_2d904188f3f2838d.text: You will also learn how to drink them like a local, and why Cologne and Düsseldorf love to tease each other.

lxc_20886738f97fb0f9.text: Kölsch is a pale, clear and light beer from Cologne.

lxc_dcc0b139eaadb9de.text: It is top-fermented, which means the yeast works at warmer temperatures.

lxc_babb5910f06664d6.text: That method gives the beer a fresh, slightly fruity taste.

lxc_97de0706a25b91be.text: Brewing has a long history in the city, and Cologne's brewers' guild dates back to 1396.

lxc_2adf286d5700c254.text: Not every beer can call itself Kölsch.

lxc_b36fd3eb17914b74.text: In 1986, Cologne's breweries signed the Kölsch Konvention, an agreement that defines what the beer is and where it can be brewed.

lxc_b17d3818f040b256.text: Later, the European Union gave the name geographical protection.

lxc_cfcb76484aacacf4.text: So Kölsch is like Champagne: the place is part of the name.

lxc_f8111b098f21ebe8.text: The word is also the name of the local dialect, so people joke that it is the only language you can drink.

lxc_9ea3a51a3c2c75fd.text: The drinking customs are just as important.

lxc_5a63d2b8ef65ff74.text: Kölsch comes in a narrow 0.2-litre glass called a Stange.

lxc_791e2876841f2bf2.text: The waiter is called a Köbes, and he carries the glasses in a round tray called a Kranz.

lxc_aa43d4f1452f1a7b.text: When your glass is empty, the Köbes usually replaces it without asking.

lxc_15d2e4e942a466a2.text: He also marks each beer on your beer mat.

lxc_2688a9a19f2e0263.text: To stop, you put the beer mat on top of your glass.

lxc_3fe85a046fdefbc9.text: Famous brewery pubs in the Old Town include Früh, founded in 1904, and Päffgen, founded in 1883.

lxc_9443f798f89b8131.text: The beer stays cold and fresh, and the quick refills keep the room lively.

lxc_626d1d63e02fd30b.text: Many visitors think "Alt" means old beer, but that is a mistake.

lxc_e0b5a019a3b1541d.text: "Alt" refers to the old way of brewing, with top-fermenting yeast, the same basic method used for Kölsch.

lxc_abe58be425f7c440.text: The result is very different, though.

lxc_e65cc9345fa310fb.text: Altbier is dark copper or brown, with a stronger malt flavour and more bitterness.

lxc_f04eed62af28b2a2.text: Altbier is usually served in a small glass, often 0.25 litres.

lxc_4c1f38cccf08978b.text: As in Cologne, the waiters are called Köbes.

lxc_417c459d3497dafa.text: The heart of this culture is the Old Town, which locals call "the longest bar in the world" because it has so many pubs close together.

lxc_b2fa630ea340e00e.text: Traditional brewery pubs there include Schumacher (1838), Füchschen (1848) and Uerige (1862).

lxc_9bf6f99d784286ce.text: Each one brews its own Altbier.

lxc_f63e7cc033a90e3c.text: The two cities are only about 40 kilometres apart.

lxc_5f1d14b5dc74b7f9.text: Their beers use a similar method and have similar customs, but they look and taste different.

lxc_8b7f11656123f84f.text: Small differences between close neighbours often create the strongest feelings.

lxc_cd3535269dbd7d60.text: The rivalry also appears in Carnival and football.

lxc_9df7384fba08d91b.text: Cologne is the bigger city, but Düsseldorf is the state capital.

lxc_f99ff96285fb6bf2.text: Locals often joke that you should never order Kölsch in Düsseldorf or Altbier in Cologne.

lxc_58927afaa26765e4.text: Mostly, this is humour, not real hostility.

lxc_35cff387bb51d36d.text: It is a city in the Ruhr, a region that became rich from coal mining and steel.

lxc_dd4102bdf07565a7.text: In the second half of the 1800s, many people did hard, hot work there, and local breweries grew quickly.

lxc_dba3c2903b857209.text: Dortmunder Export developed in this world.

lxc_e250b2e9962dad5a.text: It is a bottom-fermented pale lager, a little stronger than many everyday beers, with more malt and less bitterness than a Pils.

lxc_9c5c138a683b34d3.text: The name "Export" shows that it was made to be sold far beyond the city.

lxc_344761319d0d6a33.text: For a long time, Dortmund was one of the biggest brewing cities in Europe.

lxc_bc817a6a401c524b.text: Famous names include Dortmunder Actien-Brauerei (DAB), founded in 1868, and Dortmunder Union.

lxc_d098654bdd735d01.text: You can still see this history in the Dortmunder U. This former Union brewery building has a large glowing "U" on its roof, and today it is a centre for art and culture.

lxc_cf45ba74de6bdb27.text: As heavy industry declined and Pils became more popular, Export lost much of its importance.

lxc_ceecd19116103a35.text: The Ruhr's last coal mine closed in 2018.

lxc_1089ee76d6766fc0.text: So in Dortmund, you will not find a strict glass ritual like Cologne's.

lxc_78b5ca92056b0a75.text: The beer's meaning is in its story: it was the drink of an industrial city at work.
